items.headline: U.S. Stocks Climb as Earnings Week Kicks Off and Fed Meeting Looms
items.summary: U.S. equities are largely trending higher today, rebounding from last week's losses, as investors prepare for a busy week of major corporate earnings reports from tech giants and a highly anticipated Federal Reserve policy meeting. Easing oil prices are providing some relief, though concerns about the sustainability of AI spending continue to influence market sentiment.

items.headline: Xencor Rallies on Positive Kidney Cancer Drug Data
items.summary: Biopharmaceutical company Xencor ($XNCR) saw significant gains in early trading after announcing positive Phase 1 data for its experimental kidney cancer drug XmAb819, showing a 45.5% confirmed response rate in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Meeting and Big Tech Earnings Dominate the Week Ahead
items.summary: Investors are closely watching for the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday, with widespread expectations for interest rates to remain unchanged. Additionally, a slate of major earnings reports from companies like Microsoft ($MSFT), Alphabet ($GOOGL), and Amazon ($AMZN) this week will be key in assessing the market's direction, particularly concerning the outlook for AI spending and cloud growth.

items.headline: Oil Prices Retreat, Providing Market Breathing Room
items.summary: Brent crude futures are trending lower today after a sharp rise last week, falling towards $109 per barrel in morning trading before fluctuating. This easing in oil prices is contributing to the overall positive sentiment in the stock market, particularly benefiting sectors with high fuel costs like airlines.

items.headline: AI Spending Under Scrutiny Amid Market Swings
items.summary: Concerns persist regarding the sustainability and profitability of massive investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure. This sentiment was highlighted by Meta Platforms' announcement of plans to raise $95 billion to fund its AI ambitions, leading to a dip in its stock price today.

items.headline: Brazilian Election Results Impact Latin American Stocks
items.summary: Brazilian financial services companies experienced significant declines in early trading following the presidential runoff election in Brazil, where incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated Flávio Bolsonaro. XP Inc. ($XP) tumbled over 50%, and Nu Holdings ($NU) sank 25%, reflecting market reaction to the election outcome.
